# USC Digital Folklore Archives

> > A digital collection of folklore, folk traditions, and oral narratives from diverse cultures including Chinese-American, Hawaiian, Yoruba, Japanese, and American regional traditions.

The USC Digital Folklore Archives documents and preserves folklore collected primarily from Southern California communities, including tales, legends, superstitions, customs, and traditions from immigrant communities, indigenous cultures, and local student populations. The collection emphasizes multicultural voices and lived experiences across the United States.

## Key Topics

- Oral tradition and storytelling
- Chinese-American folklore and customs
- Hawaiian mythology and superstitions
- Urban legends and contemporary folklore
- Childhood games and playground culture
- Märchen (fairy tales) from global traditions
- Folk medicine and remedies
- Regional American customs
- Immigrant community traditions
- Yoruba and Nigerian folklore
- Japanese folktales
- College and student folklore
- Superstitions and belief systems
- Gift-giving customs and rituals

## Myths and Legends

- [Myth – Hawaiian | USC Digital Folklore Archives](https://folklore.usc.edu/myth-hawaiian): Hawaiian demigod Maui sun-snaring origin myth from Martha Beckwith
- [Mythology | USC Digital Folklore Archives](https://folklore.usc.edu/mythology): Hindu mythology about Lord Shiva and cannabis in Vedic texts
- [Legend – Beckett, Massachusetts | USC Digital Folklore Archives](https://folklore.usc.edu/legend-beckett-massachusetts): Camp Greylock clown horror legend from Massachusetts summer camp
- [Legend – Manhattan Beach, California | USC Digital Folklore Archives](https://folklore.usc.edu/legend-manhattan-beach-california): Manhattan Beach naming origin legend featuring coin flip myth
- [Contemporary Legend – Nevada | USC Digital Folklore Archives](https://folklore.usc.edu/contemporary-legend-nevada): Liberace haunted mansion ghost legend from Las Vegas, Nevada

## Märchen and Folktales

- [Märchen – Yoruba | USC Digital Folklore Archives](https://folklore.usc.edu/marchen-yoruba-2): Yoruba trickster tale featuring Ijapa tortoise from Nigerian folklore
- [Märchen – Japanese | USC Digital Folklore Archives](https://folklore.usc.edu/marchen-japanese): Japanese Crab and Monkey fairytale from Pasadena collection
- [Tale | USC Digital Folklore Archives](https://folklore.usc.edu/tale-3): Little Miss Muffet nursery rhyme variation from Manhattan Beach

## Traditions and Customs

- [Tradition – New Orleans, LA | USC Digital Folklore Archives](https://folklore.usc.edu/tradition-new-orleans-la): New Orleans above-ground burial tradition and Marie Laveau voodoo
- [Tradition – Chinese | USC Digital Folklore Archives](https://folklore.usc.edu/tradition-chinese-3): Chinese New Year Hungbau red envelope tradition from Los Angeles
- [Gift Exchange Custom | USC Digital Folklore Archives](https://folklore.usc.edu/gift-exchange-custom): Chinese-American white elephant Christmas gift exchange from Hermosa Beach
- [Custom – Oregon | USC Digital Folklore Archives](https://folklore.usc.edu/custom-oregon-2): Catholic church hat etiquette custom from Portland, Oregon

## Superstitions and Folk Medicine

- [Superstition – Hawaii | USC Digital Folklore Archives](https://folklore.usc.edu/superstition-hawaii-2): Hawaiian Pele goddess volcanic rock bad luck superstition
- [Folk Medicine – American | USC Digital Folklore Archives](https://folklore.usc.edu/folk-medicine-american): African-American hangover remedy folk medicine from San Francisco

## Children's Folklore and Games

- [Playground Song – United States | USC Digital Folklore Archives](https://folklore.usc.edu/playground-song-united-states): Circle-circle-dot-dot cootie shot playground rhyme from US schools
- [Riddle/Joke – United States of America | USC Digital Folklore Archives](https://folklore.usc.edu/riddlejoke-%e2%80%93-united-states-of-america): Chinese-American elementary school riddle from Los Angeles student culture
- [Riddle/Game | USC Digital Folklore Archives](https://folklore.usc.edu/riddlegame): Around-the-world word pattern riddle game from San Francisco

## Jokes and Humor

- [Joke | USC Digital Folklore Archives](https://folklore.usc.edu/joke-5): Life stages aging humor joke from Long Beach, California
- [Stereotype | USC Digital Folklore Archives](https://folklore.usc.edu/stereotype): Mexican stereotype blason populaire from Belize student in LA
- [Family Proverb – Saratoga, California | USC Digital Folklore Archives](https://folklore.usc.edu/family-proverb-saratoga-california): Zager family proverb about trust using card-playing metaphor
